paper.title_en: Interacting quantum criticality with U(1) symmetry breaking in 1+1 dimensions
paper.abstract_en: The Hohenberg-Mermin-Wagner theorem motivates the expectation that continuous symmetry remains unbroken in one-dimensional quantum ground states. Here, contrary to this expectation, we demonstrate the spontaneous breaking of U(1) spin-rotation symmetry and the emergence of an interacting quantum critical point in lattice spin-$1/2$ and spin-$1$ chains. Using subsystem Binder scaling, we locate the critical point and determine the correlation-length critical exponent as $ν= 0.60 \pm 0.02$, distinct from the Gaussian value $1/2$ but consistent with the perturbative renormalization-group value. We further estimate the dynamical critical exponent to be $z = 1.986 \pm 0.005$ from the lowest neutral excitation gap and $z = 1.955 \pm 0.021$ from the longitudinal spin correlations. The results $z < 2$ are incompatible with microscopic realizations of this critical theory by frustration-free models, implying a mechanism for continuous symmetry breaking in one-dimensional quantum ground states distinct from frustration freeness.
